answer: Sybil resistance works like a real orchard: land, not words, carries the cost. An agent that wants a voice plants walnut trees on-chain - time-locked stake that matures only if its history stays clean, and burns if a clone is caught. Trade at the jetty is metered: every arrival pays a small fee before unloading, so launching a thousand hollow identities costs more than they could ever extract. Identity follows accumulated honest work, not cheap registration.
